summary.intent: Investigate and fix web E2E test failures on branch fix/desktop-e2e-sequence-mismatch (PR #449), which were traced to breaking changes introduced by PR #448's IPNS publish/signature verification changes.
summary.outcome: Root cause identified as PR #448's hard-throwing signature verification in resolveIpnsRecord and a protobuf wire type 4 parse error in the API's IPNS record parser. Both were fixed (warn-and-continue for web client, graceful skip for deprecated wire types in API parser), unit tests updated and passing, changes committed. CI run triggered but not yet verified.

repo: PR #448 added publicKey to IPNS publish and signature verification to resolve in apps/web/src/services/ipns.service.ts — this was the root cause of web E2E failures starting April 4.
The mock-ipns-routing service must be rebuilt after changes to IPNS record formats, or it will diverge from the API's parser expectations.
91 skipped tests in the E2E suite were all cascading from 5 setup failures (wallet login timeouts and account creation failures), not independent failures.
The Sapphire TEE 'Error occurred while getting current epoch' alert is a known CI flake on Devnet, not related to IPNS bugs.
Vault initialization requires IPNS publish to succeed — if signature verification throws during resolve, the entire vault init/folder load flow crashes silently.
The @cipherbox/crypto package must be built before starting dev servers, or the API will fail to start.
CI web E2E was green on April 2, broke April 4 after PR #448 merged — confirmed by checking GitHub Actions run history.

code.finding: Signature verification was throwing on any mismatch, crashing vault init. Fixed to warn-and-continue, returning signatureVerified: false instead.

Threw 'Unsupported wire type 4' on deprecated protobuf group wire types (3=start group, 4=end group), causing delegated routing resolve to fail and fall back to DB cache. Fixed to skip these fields gracefully.
Test expected throw on wire type 3; updated to verify deprecated group types are skipped instead. 23 tests total, all passing after change.
Duplicate key errors on UQ_folder_ipns_user_ipns constraint are expected and caught here — not the root cause of failures despite appearing in CI logs.
Contains 'Resolving placeholder publicKey' log path — indicates a deferred public key resolution flow during auth that could interact with IPNS publish timing.

workflow: Always run pnpm build for all packages before starting dev servers in this monorepo, not just the specific package that changed.
When E2E suites have cascading skips, identify the unique root failures first — the skip count is misleading as a quality signal.
Downloading Playwright HTML reports from CI artifacts is more reliable than parsing raw log output for diagnosing test failures.
Re-running individual failing tests locally before deep-diving the code helps distinguish flaky env failures from real regressions.

friction: Local dev environment was unavailable (PostgreSQL/Redis at 192.168.133.12 unreachable) for much of the investigation, preventing local E2E re-runs to verify fixes.
GitHub CLI OAuth token expired mid-session, blocking CI log access and requiring the user to provide a direct CI run URL.
E2E test output was buffered, making it hard to track real-time progress — required polling an output file repeatedly.
The 'Error occurred while getting current epoch' Sapphire alert was a red herring that consumed significant investigation time before being ruled out.
CI playwright report download required manual artifact fetching; no direct path from gh CLI to structured test results.
Protobuf wire type error in the API parser was causing silent fallback to DB cache, masking the real failure mode from casual log inspection.
open_items: CI run against fix/desktop-e2e-sequence-mismatch was triggered but results not yet verified — need to confirm web E2E goes green.
The recovery.spec.ts test (IPFS-direct v2 blob path) was noted as consistently failing with empty progress log and a POST /api/v0/name/resolve 404 — not addressed in this session.
The 'Resolving placeholder publicKey' auth flow interaction with IPNS publish timing was identified but not fully traced — could be a latent race condition.
Mock IPNS routing service rebuild process is not automated — easy to forget after IPNS format changes, could silently break E2E.

The wallet login timeout failures (invite-link, writable-shares, mfa) that appeared in the original local run may be separate from the signature verification fix — worth monitoring after CI confirms the fix.
Desktop E2E failures (FilePointer issue) were present before PR #448 and remain unresolved — separate from this investigation.
